corpusSummary: This corpus of 2026 social-science papers on large language models spans human–AI interaction, education, health, climate, and AI-as-research-tool. It centers on trust, representation, safety, and ethics, while highlighting LLMs as analytic aids, co-ideation partners, and governance tools. Recurring topics include misinformation, bias, cultural sensitivity, and the social implications of deploying AI in diverse contexts.

themes.name: Trust and humanness in AI interactions
themes.description: Explores how users judge trust, perceived humanness, and influence in AI-supported counseling, relationship advice, and everyday decision contexts.

themes.name: AI as research tool and methodological governance
themes.description: Documents frameworks, workflows, and governance considerations for integrating LLMs into social-science research, policy analysis, and data-driven inquiry.

themes.name: AI in education and learning across ages
themes.description: Encompasses AI-assisted learning, literacy development, and assessment practices across students, teachers, and older adults.

themes.name: Safety, bias, and misinformation in LLM deployment
themes.description: Examines model fairness, risk of misinformation, content safety, and the reliability of AI outputs across domains including health, libraries, and media.
